name: erdos_mollin_walsh
claim_latex: There do not exist three consecutive positive integers $(n, n+1, n+2)$ all of which are powerful (a positive integer $m$ is powerful iff every prime $p \mid m$ satisfies $p^2 \mid m$).

given_facts.statement: For all $n \leq 10^{14}$, no triple $(n, n+1, n+2)$ has all three powerful.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: POSITIVE existence claim about the *non-existence* of triples up to a finite bound. The bound is an UPPER bound on $n$ (the smallest possibly-powerful triple, if any exists, has $n > 10^{14}$). Treating this as a proof of the conjecture is a sign error: it only rules out small witnesses.
given_facts.citation: stated as F1 in the project prompt; matches Mollin–Walsh-style computational searches. CAUTION (2026-07-11 literature audit): no published source stating an explicit exhaustive-search bound for consecutive powerful triples was verifiable; the 10^14 figure should be treated as a working assumption, not a citable fact.
warns: F1 only rules out small $n$. A witness must have $n > 10^{14}$. Any chain that concludes 'EMW is proved' from F1 alone is BLOCKING.
The 10^14 bound itself is UNVERIFIED in the literature — do not cite it in a writeup without independent verification.

given_facts.statement: Tsz Ho Chan (2025): there are no consecutive powerful triples $(n, n+1, n+2)$ in which the middle term is a perfect cube and each outer term has exactly one prime raised to an odd power. A companion 2025 preprint eliminates a further family around cubes with prime-square factors.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: NON-EXISTENCE for restricted structural families only. Says nothing about triples outside these families; the general conjecture remains open.
given_facts.citation: T. H. Chan, 'A note on three consecutive powerful numbers', INTEGERS 25 (2025) #A7, arXiv:2503.21485 (via Pell equations, elliptic curves, second-order recurrences); arXiv:2507.16828 (2025).
warns: Structural-family results like F4 are the current state of the art — a full proof must handle families F4 does not cover.

given_facts.statement: Granville–Mollin–Walsh: the abc conjecture implies that the set of $n$ with $(n, n+1, n+2)$ all powerful is *finite*.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: FINITENESS, not non-existence. Even under abc, finitely many counterexamples may exist. F2 does NOT imply EMW; it conditionally implies a quantitative version (an explicit upper bound on $n$).
warns: Reading F2 as 'abc implies EMW' is a sign error: abc gives finiteness but not zero counterexamples.

given_facts.statement: If $(n, n+1, n+2)$ are all powerful with $n+1 = a^2 b$ ($b$ squarefree), then the gap structure forces $a, b$ to satisfy a Pell-type equation $X^2 - DY^2 = \pm 1$ for $D$ depending on the squarefree parts of $n, n+1, n+2$. The number of solutions to such Pell equations is finite for each fixed $D$.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: FINITELY MANY per Pell instance, but $D$ ranges over infinitely many squarefree triples. F3 does NOT imply finiteness of the union over all $D$. Concluding 'finitely many EMW triples' from F3 alone is a sign error.
warns: F3 controls Pell solutions for fixed squarefree parts. The aggregate over varying $D$ is unbounded; F3 alone is not enough to close EMW.

witness_schema.n: int >= 2 — the candidate smallest element; verifier checks n, n+1, n+2 are all powerful
witness_schema.claimed_smallest: int (optional) — agent's claim for the smallest powerful triple; verifier recomputes

status_audited: 2026-07-11 — confirmed OPEN as of July 2026 (best partial results: Chan 2025 structural families, F4).
note: Erdős–Mollin–Walsh conjecture. Two-track problem: Track 1 search loop hunts for a witness $n$ via sieving; Track 2 proof loop attempts a proof under the F1+F2+F3 ledger. Witness is a single integer $n$ with $n, n+1, n+2$ all powerful — verifier factors all three by trial division up to sqrt(max), checks every prime factor has multiplicity >= 2. Score = the smallest such $n$ (chosen so larger witnesses don't strictly outrank smaller ones — a single witness suffices). Computer-verified up to ~10^14 via Heath-Brown / Mollin–Walsh; any witness has $n > 10^{14}$, so the verifier must accept arbitrary-precision integers.

ideation_lenses.name: pell-recurrences
ideation_lenses.description: Consecutive powerful PAIRS come from Pell-type recurrences (8,9; 288,289; ...). Study the obstruction to extending a Pell pair to a triple; recurrence structure modulo squarefull constraints.

ideation_lenses.name: elliptic-mordell
ideation_lenses.description: A powerful triple forces integral points on explicit Mordell/elliptic models (powerful m = a^2 b^3). Leverage integral-point finiteness, explicit curve computations, and rank bounds to exclude the parametrized families.

ideation_lenses.name: padic-local
ideation_lenses.description: Local obstructions: among n, n+1, n+2 the even members must be 0 mod 4 (2-adic valuation 1 kills powerfulness), pinning n mod 4; mine mod-p^2 conditions systematically for an outright contradiction or strong density savings.

ideation_lenses.name: abc-heights
ideation_lenses.description: abc kills all large triples. Make the implication quantitative (radical/height inequalities) to bound any counterexample's size, then complement with finite search below the bound.

ideation_lenses.name: sieve-density
ideation_lenses.description: Powerful numbers count ~ c x^(1/2). Bound triple correlations by sieve/second-moment methods; even modest savings on pair correlations constrain where a triple could live.

ideation_lenses.name: counterexample-first
ideation_lenses.description: Parametrize candidate triples through squarefull factorizations and Pell-pair extensions; the witness verifier decides any concrete candidate.
